# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 11 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**11:1** I thank You, Lord, for You have done astonishing things with mere dust -- with a lump of clay You have displayed Your power.

**11:2** And what am I? I was scooped from the dirt and molded from mud. I was shaped as a spring of filth and shame,

**11:3** a pile of dust soaked in water, a house of shadows, a clay figure destined to crumble back to earth

**11:4** when its time comes, traveling the road all dust must travel. What can the clay say back? What can a thing shaped by another's hands

**11:5** possibly understand? You have done astonishing things with dust -- with a thing of clay You have displayed Your power.

**11:6** How can anyone born of a woman stand in Your presence? Kneaded from dirt, destined to feed the worms,

**11:7** nothing but molded mud yearning to return to the ground. What can the clay say? What can a handmade thing

**11:8** possibly understand?

**11:9** Yet You -- You have placed a song of gratitude in my mouth and words of praise on my tongue, and my lips overflow with rejoicing,

**11:10** and I will sing of Your faithful love and Your strength all day long; I will never stop blessing Your name.

**11:11** I will proclaim Your splendor to the world, and the richness of Your goodness fills my soul with delight.

**11:12** For I know that truth lives in Your word, justice rests in Your hand, all wisdom dwells in Your mind,

**11:13** all strength resides in Your power, and every form of glory belongs to You.

**11:14** In Your anger come crushing judgments, but in Your goodness overflows abundant forgiveness,

**11:15** and Your mercy reaches everyone You have chosen.

**11:16** You have let them glimpse the truth of Your purposes and opened their eyes to Your breathtaking mysteries.

**11:17** For Your own honor You have washed a human being clean of sin, so that he can set himself apart

**11:18** from every vile corruption and every stain of betrayal, to be gathered together

**11:19** with Your faithful ones and counted among Your consecrated people -- lifting the worm from the grave-dust

**11:20** to the eternal assembly, turning a warped spirit toward Your wisdom,

**11:21** so that he may stand in Your presence alongside the undying host and the spirits of insight,

**11:22** to be made new with everything that exists and will exist, sharing the joy of all who truly know.

**11:23** But what is a human being compared to all this? What can a creature of clay accomplish that is truly wonderful?

**11:24** From the moment of birth he lives entangled in wrongdoing, and until his hair turns white he remains trapped in guilt.

**11:25** I know that no mortal owns righteousness, and no human being walks a flawless path on his own;

**11:26** only the Most High God performs truly righteous acts, and a person's path has no firm footing

**11:27** unless God's own spirit steadies him, making the road straight for the human race,

**11:28** so that every creature of His may witness the force of His strength and the depth of His mercy

**11:29** toward all those He has chosen.

**11:30** As for me -- shaking and trembling overwhelmed me, every bone in my body cracked apart,

**11:31** my heart turned to liquid like wax near a flame, my knees buckled like water cascading down a hillside,

**11:32** when I remembered my own guilt and the faithlessness passed down from my ancestors, when wicked people attacked Your covenant

**11:33** and worthless people defied Your word. I said to myself: My sin

**11:34** has surely banished me from Your covenant. But the moment I remembered the power of Your hand and the ocean of Your mercy,

**11:35** I gathered my strength. I stood up. My spirit braced itself against the assault,

**11:36** because I anchored myself to Your faithful love and the wealth of Your compassion. For You wipe away wrongdoing

**11:37** and scrub a human being clean of guilt through Your justice.

---
*PNEUMA notes: Column 11 is excellently preserved. This hymn is a profound meditation on human smallness and divine generosity. The clay/dust imagery draws from the same well as Genesis 2 and Job. The emotional arc -- from self-abasement to trembling to courageous trust -- is one of the most moving passages in the Scrolls. Rendered for contemporary readers while preserving the raw emotional power of the Hebrew.*
